notes: Contracts: 'country' is the vendor's country (country_of_vendor), i.e. where the supplier is based, not where the work is done; a U.S. firm supplying a Canadian base counts as United States. Value is the contract's current total value booked on its award date, so multi-year deals count in full in the window they were signed.

Grants and contributions: 'country' is the recipient's mailing address (recipient_country), not where the money is spent. UN agencies and international NGOs are mostly addressed in New York, Geneva, Rome, Vienna, Paris or London, so those cities' countries collect money spent elsewhere. Value is the agreement's current total (latest amendment), dated by the original agreement start date, as on the federal page. Canadian NGOs delivering aid abroad are addressed in Canada and are not counted here.

IATI (Global Affairs Canada only): 'country' is the activity's recipient country as GAC reports it, the best measure of where aid goes. Money is actual disbursements in the window by transaction date (a flow), not agreement totals (a commitment), so it is not comparable dollar for dollar with grants. Multi-country activities are split by GAC's recipient-country percentages; the share GAC assigns to a region rather than a country is listed as unplaced under the region's name. Other departments' aid (e.g. Finance, IRCC) is not in this file.

Do not add the sources together: GAC's aid appears both in the grants file (by agreement) and in IATI (by disbursement). 831 of the 1017 GAC activities with disbursements after the election ($3.0B of $3.5B) match a GAC agreement in the grants file by project number (any start date, any recipient address); 87 of the 248 foreign-addressed GAC grants signed after the election ($0.7B of $3.0B) are already IATI activities; the rest are mostly new multi-year institutional pledges (Global Fund, Gavi, IFAD, African Development Bank) not yet in GAC's IATI files and assessed contributions to the UN, NATO, OECD and similar bodies.

Keyword flags are whole-word matches on English text (French only when no English is given): W women/girls, M men/boys, G gender, L LGBTQ2+ terms. A flag means the words appear in the title, description, program name or expected results, not that the money is targeted at that group. Contract descriptions are standard category labels (e.g. 'Management consulting'), so contracts almost never carry a flag. P and S are GAC's own OECD gender-equality policy marker (principal objective / significant objective) and exist for IATI records only.
Gender Inequality Index: UNDP Human Development Report, 2023 values; rank 1 = most equal among the 172 countries with a value. Lower is more equal.
Grants to individuals with a foreign address (mostly NSERC, SSHRC and CIHR fellowships held abroad and Canadian athletes training abroad) are counted under that country but not named.
3 foreign contracts of $100M or more were awarded after the election, worth $0.7B of the $1.7B contracts total; they are multi-year deals booked on the award date.
Countries with money but no shape on the 1:50m map (listed, not drawn): Gibraltar (GIB), Martinique (MTQ), United States Minor Outlying Islands (UMI).
